source: Edited directly in pull requests; validated by node scripts/work-packages.mjs validate (part of npm run check).

packages.title: Resolve auth and multi-party access contracts
packages.goal: Research secure classic authentication, owner/participant access and employment lifecycle before implementation.
steps: Review auth library/provider options with current official sources.
Propose account-link/recovery threat model and multi-party policy table.
Propose immutable RFQ/quote and grant transition contracts for FND-002.
acceptance: Password primary and one name field preserved.
One employer UI, personally owned projects and counterpart private fields modeled.
RLS role/bypass and revocation risks explicitly tested in planned cases.

packages.title: Turn references into screen contracts
packages.goal: Inventory current references and missing states before drawing or implementing full interfaces.
steps: Review every selected reference and corrective note.
Define screen audience/data/actions/empty/error/mobile/focus contracts.
Submit latest workspace for explicit design review; preserve unapproved status until decision.
acceptance: Exact seven public sections and stable workspace destinations.
Single avatar/one company/single floating assistant constraints preserved.
No synthetic customer/metric claims migrated to real seed data.

packages.title: Freeze v1 domain and API contracts
packages.goal: Create validated schemas and API examples that independently unblock backend and frontend.
steps: Review research proposals and resolve blocking model decisions.
Define schema validation, API errors/revisions/idempotency, projections, exact money and immutable version contracts.
Publish contract fixtures for pure participant, mixed buyer/seller and personal project.
Integrator alone updates shared dependencies/configuration when necessary.
acceptance: Published RFQ versions immutable; invitations and quote versions pin rfq_version_id.
Old quote against qty10 v1 cannot silently compare/accept as qty100 v2.
Unknown/acknowledged/final external outcomes and crash reconciliation distinct.
Runtime validation and forbidden-field contract tests pass.
Freeze retrieval schemas, audience intersections, model/generation IDs, structured complete-domain facts, citations and serialized egress/delivery policy with runtime validators.

packages.title: Implement initial identity/access persistence
packages.goal: Deliver small executable SQL migrations and repository ports for identity/company/project participation.
steps: Select typed query adapter with ADR proposal; request root dependency change through integrator.
Implement migration runner/checksum ledger and initial XOR-owner/active-membership/participation tables.
Create restricted runtime role and seed synthetic fixtures only.
Test empty/upgrade migrations and policy constraints under real runtime credentials.
acceptance: No schema auto-sync or applied-migration editing.
Actual PostgreSQL tests cover cross-company/personal project/revoked member.
RLS bypass roles/views/definer functions explicitly considered.

Transfer exclusive packages/data ownership first to BE-001 for common admission/revocation, then to RAG-201 for retrieval migrations; no concurrent writers. Trusted transaction-local DB identity and missing/pool-reused identity denial tested.

packages.title: Implement identity and object policy slice
packages.goal: Build classic auth and scoped project/company access using accepted contracts.
steps: Implement auth/session/reset/link adapter using fakes for external providers.
Implement membership end, owner/leader separation and participation policy.

After DATA-001 acceptance, take exclusive ownership of packages/data to implement the common admission/revocation primitive in packages/data/admission, its ordered migrations and identity-revocation integration. Bind bounded provider dispatch/delivery to current policy, exact payload digest, provider policy/model/data class; serialize admission with committed revocation.
Add public/private serializers and command authorization.
Wire modules through an integration request if the composition path is outside the package's paths.
acceptance: No auto-link by unverified email; no privilege from buyer preference.
Former employee loses company authority; own identity persists.
Public projects expose no private attachments/prices/messages.
Object matrix and session/revocation tests pass.
Common admission primitive and identity revocation share one authoritative linearization contract, verified across API/worker nodes before RAG-201 may dispatch embeddings.

Revoke between preflight and actual embedding dispatch denies new admission; expiry, wrong provider/model/policy/data class/query-vs-document permit, replay and pooled missing identity fail closed. Already admitted bytes are explicitly outside recall guarantee.

packages.title: Create independent accessible design system
packages.goal: Create canonical editable logo, tokens and accessible components for standalone development.
steps: Recreate canonical editable brand under explicit design task with provenance.
Define typography/spacing/color and interaction states; keep Russian locale keys.
Build semantic accessible navigation/dialog/form/table primitives.
Validate desktop/mobile/focus/contrast; propose workspace review.
acceptance: Three blue squares and black stacked Russian wordmark; no logo drift.
Accessible icon-only controls and overlay without page reflow.
Independent system now; Orbit compatibility deferred until post-client-approval handover.
Human approval evidence separate from implementation checks.
Specify Russian retrieval source/citation/current/historical/partial/no-answer/revoked states from frozen contracts.

packages.title: Implement public and workspace shells
packages.goal: Implement accepted navigation/layout and account/onboarding screens against contract fixtures.
steps: Use shared tokens/locale and accepted schemas.
Build public resource shell and daily workspace with simultaneous buying/selling.
Implement classic login/signup/onboarding UI with fake API contract transport until backend integrated.
Cover responsive/empty/error/permission states and clearly label fixtures in development.
acceptance: Exact public/workspace IA; no role/company switch, inbox or duplicated avatar.
Signup single name; skip optional onboarding; no forced INN.
Russian UI; mobile and keyboard checks; mock state never called live functionality.

packages.title: Prepare first-class RAG architecture and deterministic contracts
packages.goal: Document the explicitly authorized RAG foundation without provisioning inference or claiming runtime quality.
steps: Reconcile earlier vector deferral with required hybrid retrieval.
Define source/field/party authority, citations, egress and derived-data lifecycle.
Add deterministic fake fixtures and future evidence gates; submit exact candidate.
acceptance: Architecture/source register/contracts/fixtures/DAG consistent; no source image changes.
Independent exact-head review and check required before integration; CI account blocker remains explicit.
One-off maintainer-authorized change before merge documented; integrator bookkeeping scope unchanged.

packages.title: Resolve corpus, model and retrieval evaluation contract
packages.goal: Specify rights-cleared gold corpus and model/config selection evidence before shared contracts freeze.
steps: Inventory actual permitted source shapes and expected load.
Compare pinned multilingual model candidates using authorized resources only.
Document benchmark protocol and immutable configuration proposal for FND-002.
acceptance: Corpus strata, rights, relevance labels, version/as-of and no-answer gold reviewed.
Model revisions/license/dimensions/limits/hardware/egress resolved or explicitly blocked; no fabricated real-model results.
Proposed quality/capacity thresholds reviewed; external vector store remains evidence-based.

packages.title: Platform administration research and screen contracts
packages.goal: Define the essence, capability map, roles, screens, data/audit requirements, risks and implementation plan of the staff administration surface.
steps: Study comparable products and admin frameworks.
Map capabilities, roles and separation of duties.
Write screen contracts, data/audit requirements and the implementation proposal.
acceptance: Separate staff surface; no implicit private access; no ranking controls; audited actions.

packages.title: Country-pack model, registration identifier and currency abstraction; remove Russia-only assumptions
packages.goal: A country-agnostic engine: packs carry locales, currency, registration identifier, entity types, regions, formats, legal templates and data residency; ИНН/ОГРН and RUB are gone outside the optional ru locale.
steps: Create packages/country-packs with a Zod schema, packs uz/ge/am/az, the restricted-places list and a validator test.
Replace RegionKey with ISO 3166-2 codes from the pack; replace inn/ogrn with pack identifier kinds; format money with Intl in the pack currency.
Re-base the demo fixtures on Uzbekistan (regions, STIR, UZS); keep data synthetic and labelled.
Remove Russian integrations and plans from code and docs.
acceptance: No ИНН, ОГРН or RUB outside the optional ru locale.
packages/country-packs test validates every pack; restricted codes cannot be enabled.
npm run check green at the candidate SHA.

packages.title: i18n engine and country selector
packages.goal: Multilingual UI with English as default and fallback; the country is chosen on first visit, kept in the profile and URL, and switchable in the header.
steps: Request-scoped locale on the server, provider for client components, per-locale dictionaries with en fallback and a missing-key test.
Cookie plus ?country=/?lang= resolution in proxy.ts; first-visit selector listing enabled packs only; header switcher.
Fonts that render Georgian and Armenian; no RTL.
acceptance: Every screen renders in each enabled locale without untranslated keys (test).
The selector never lists a restricted place.
Screenshots of the selector and switcher.

packages.title: Uzbekistan pack end to end
packages.goal: Every screen in uz-Latn with native-quality copy, UZS everywhere, UZ registration identifier (STIR) and ISO 3166-2:UZ regions; demo data for Uzbekistan.
steps: Write the uz-Latn dictionaries for the design system and the app; review for native quality, no machine-translation placeholders.
Localize the demo fixtures for Uzbekistan.
Record screenshots of the UZ flow.
acceptance: Screenshots of the UZ flow in uz-Latn.
No untranslated keys in uz-Latn.
Identifier and region facts cite their sources.

packages.title: Georgia pack
packages.goal: Georgia pack: ka locale, GEL, identification code, ISO 3166-2:GE regions.
steps: Complete the pack and the ka dictionaries; verify identifier facts against napr.gov.ge.
acceptance: Pack validates; ka renders with Georgian-capable fonts; facts cite sources.

packages.title: Armenia pack
packages.goal: Armenia pack: hy locale, AMD, TIN, ISO 3166-2:AM regions.
steps: Complete the pack and the hy dictionaries; verify identifier facts against src.am.
acceptance: Pack validates; hy renders with Armenian-capable fonts; facts cite sources.

packages.title: Azerbaijan pack
packages.goal: Azerbaijan pack: az-Latn locale, AZN, VÖEN, ISO 3166-2:AZ regions.
steps: Complete the pack and the az-Latn dictionaries; verify identifier facts against taxes.gov.az.
acceptance: Pack validates; facts cite sources.

packages.title: Sanctions terms template, partner SDN hook, removal of Russian integrations and plans
packages.goal: Operators get a sanctions and export-controls terms section; partner onboarding carries an ownership declaration and an SDN screening hook; Russian integrations and plans are gone from docs and briefs.
steps: Write the terms template section mirroring Contribuddha Terms §3.
Add packages/compliance with the Consolidated Screening List adapter (key empty) and the ownership declaration contract.
Remove Russian integrations and plans from research, briefs and screen contracts.
acceptance: No Russian-provider adapters remain.
Screening adapter refuses to run without a key and never fakes a clear result.
Terms section present in the template.

packages.title: Migration layout for parallel slices: one directory per module, schema mirror per module
packages.goal: Let several packages add migrations at the same time without sharing a directory: the runner reads one subdirectory per module in global timestamp order, and the schema mirror is split per module.
steps: Extend loadMigrations to read the flat root (the twelve applied files stay where they are, so their ledger names and checksums do not change) plus exactly one level of module subdirectories (packages/data/migrations/<module>/); order all files globally by their 14-digit timestamp.
Fail loudly on a nested directory, a non-SQL file, a malformed name or the same file name in two directories; keep forward-only and out-of-order detection unchanged.

Move the live tables of packages/data/src/schema.ts unchanged into packages/data/src/schema/foundation.ts with an index; later slices add packages/data/src/schema/<module>.ts, and the introspection test discovers module files by listing the directory, so a slice never edits a shared file.

Document the layout and the rule "a package owns packages/data/migrations/<module>, packages/data/src/schema/<module>.ts and packages/data/src/repositories/<module>.ts" in packages/data/README.md and the migration plan.
acceptance: A migration placed in packages/data/migrations/<module>/ is applied by npm run db:migrate in a test; one placed two levels deep makes the runner fail.
The ledger of an existing database is unchanged after upgrading the runner (no re-application, no checksum mismatch; tested from the previous schema).
The schema introspection test still matches information_schema for every live table.
Two files with the same name in different module directories are rejected.

packages.title: Harden the pipeline: required database tests, audits, drift and size checks
packages.goal: Make CI fail on the gaps found in the audit instead of passing silently.
steps: Fail when database suites skip in CI (TRUSTWORK_REQUIRE_PG=1) and print a summary of skipped suites locally.
Run the design-system axe suite and add a client bundle-size budget to the browser job.
Add npm audit for runtime dependencies (fail on high), a licence allowlist check and Dependabot configuration for npm and GitHub Actions.
Verify the gitleaks download checksum; add an OpenAPI regeneration drift check.
Stop npm run check from rewriting tracked files (apps/web/next-env.d.ts); propose root configuration edits in the pull request for a maintainer to agree.
acceptance: Removing the database service from CI makes the check job fail.
An accessibility violation in a Storybook story fails CI.
A changed contract without regenerated OpenAPI fails CI.
A clean checkout stays clean after npm run check.

packages.title: Production runtime baseline: configuration guard, structured logs, readiness, telemetry, security headers
packages.goal: Make the API and web processes safe and observable to run outside a laptop without changing domain behaviour.
steps: Validate production configuration with a Zod schema: refuse to boot without AUTH_FLOW_SECRET, an https PUBLIC_ORIGIN and secure cookies; make the pool size, statement_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout configurable; align .env.example with the variables the code reads.
Replace console logging with structured JSON logs (request id, pseudonymous principal, route, status, latency, error stack) with redaction of secrets and private fields.
Add /health/live and /health/ready (database reachable, migration ledger verified, expected schema version) and align HealthSchema with the provider mode.
Add OpenTelemetry traces and metrics exported to an OTLP endpoint when configured, no-op otherwise.
Add security headers on web (apps/web/proxy.ts, nonce-based CSP) and API (HSTS, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) and configurable trusted proxy hops instead of trust-all.
acceptance: The API refuses to start in production with a missing flow secret, an http origin or insecure cookies (tested).
A forced 500 produces one JSON log line with the stack and request id and no secret or private field (tested).
Readiness fails when the database is unreachable or the ledger has a checksum mismatch.
A spoofed X-Forwarded-For from an untrusted hop does not change the client address used for limits (tested).

packages.title: Outbox relay, durable job runner and scheduler in apps/worker
packages.goal: Turn the existing outbox and job tables into a running worker so provider effects and maintenance leave the request path.
steps: Give the worker its own restricted database role with only the grants it needs (outbox, job, inbox, sweeper) in packages/data/migrations/worker; revoke the API role's SELECT on audit_event and outbox_event in the same reviewed slice.

Implement the outbox relay (claim unpublished rows with SKIP LOCKED, dispatch to typed handlers, mark published) with a handler registry keyed by event type; import contracts through package exports, not relative source paths.
Implement the job loop: lease, heartbeat, fencing-checked completion and failure, backoff, dead letters, outcome_unknown parking and an explicit reconciliation command.

Schedule maintenance: sweep_expired with intervals fixed inside the definer function, idempotency cleanup, monthly audit and outbox partitions; graceful shutdown that stops leasing and finishes or releases work.
Add fault-injection tests: kill between lease and completion, duplicate delivery, stale fencing token, clock skew.
acceptance: A worker killed mid-job never causes a second effect without reconciliation (real PostgreSQL test).
Outbox age, queue depth, lease expirations and unknown outcomes are exported as metrics.
The worker role cannot read party tables and the API role cannot read audit rows (tested).
npm run worker:demo is replaced by a worker test that consumes a real outbox row.

packages.title: Identity hardening follow-ups
packages.goal: Close review and audit follow-ups: e-mail squatting, admission revoke scoping, disabled-provider 404, lockout abuse, idempotency crash recovery and hard-coded strings in identity.
steps: Mailbox proof revokes a squatting unverified binding.
Scope admission_revoke to the caller's own scopes or maintenance; require an identity or the maintenance role for auth_disable_password (reviewed migration in packages/data/migrations/identity).
Provider callback answers 404 when providers are disabled; store a null provider display name instead of the hard-coded Russian fallback and render a localized placeholder.
Replace permanent password disable with progressive delay and owner notification; recovery or a verified session clears the counter.
Make idempotency completion atomic with the handler transaction or give in_progress records a short takeover lease; use the injected clock. (Scheduling sweep_expired moved to REL-001.)
acceptance: The squatting scenario is resolved by victim verification; tests pass on real PostgreSQL.
An attacker cannot disable another person's password by failed attempts (tested).
A crash between handler commit and bookkeeping does not block the user's retry for longer than the takeover lease (tested).
No visible string is hard-coded in apps/api (lint or test).

packages.title: Account and directory completeness: company creation, handles, lists with pagination
packages.goal: Let a real user reach the states the web shows: create a company, find their projects, browse public directories by handle.
steps: Contracts first: company creation (unclaimed; creator becomes administrator), handle rules for person, company and project (UUIDs stay the stable identifiers, ADR 012), list queries with cursor pagination.
Migrations in packages/data/migrations/directory: handle columns with uniqueness, indexes that serve the row-level policies and keyset pagination.
Implement POST /v1/companies, GET /v1/me/projects, GET /v1/people, GET /v1/companies, GET /v1/projects and lookups by handle in a new directory module (public projections only for anonymous callers).
Test negative authorization, pagination stability under concurrent inserts and query plans under the runtime role.
acceptance: A company created through the API has exactly one administrator and no claimed or verified status.
Directories never return private fields or unpublished objects; tests prove it per projection.
List queries use index scans on 100,000 synthetic rows under the runtime role.
Handles are unique per kind, changeable with a redirect record, and never reused for another subject.

packages.title: Transactional mail through the outbox with localized templates and an SMTP adapter
packages.goal: Deliver verification, recovery, invitation and security notices for real, asynchronously, in the recipient's language.
steps: Record mail intents as outbox events in the same transaction as the identity change instead of calling MailPort from handlers.
Render templates from locale files in every engine language (subject, text and HTML) with the hub brand from configuration, never a hard-coded brand.
Implement a provider-neutral SMTP adapter and keep the fake; configuration chooses one; no provider account is registered by this package.
Record delivery, bounce and complaint receipts idempotently in inbox_receipt; suppress sending to hard-bounced addresses.
Keep enumeration safety: identical HTTP timing and responses whether or not an address exists.
acceptance: Signup, recovery and invitation work end to end against a local SMTP sink in tests.
A failing mail provider never fails or slows the HTTP request (tested with a stalled sink).
Every template exists in every engine language; a missing key fails the tests.
Duplicate outbox delivery sends at most one message per intent.

packages.title: Second factor, recovery codes and elevated sessions
packages.goal: Give staff and cautious participants a second factor (TOTP and recovery codes) and an elevated-session state that the administration console, the setup wizard and support servicing require.
steps: Contracts and migrations (packages/data/migrations/identity) for second-factor enrolment, recovery codes (hashed) and session elevation with expiry.
Implement enrolment with confirmation, verification with replay protection, recovery-code use and regeneration, and notification of every change to all verified addresses.
Implement admin.session.elevate: step-up plus second factor, short expiry, bound to the session; staff routes refuse unelevated sessions.
A second-factor reset by support needs a second person and a 72-hour cooling-off (SUP-001 calls this use case).
acceptance: A reused TOTP code within its window is rejected (tested).
Recovery codes are stored only as hashes and each works once.
An unelevated or expired elevated session gets 403 on a staff route (tested).
Every factor change notifies all verified addresses through the outbox.

packages.title: Locale correctness and weight: request-scoped client locale, one dictionary per page, CLDR plurals, country-aware formats
packages.goal: Fix cross-request locale mixing, ship only the active dictionary and format numbers and dates for language plus country.
steps: Replace the module-level client store with a request-scoped React context for server rendering of client components; add a concurrent two-locale rendering test.
Remove module-level dictionary evaluation from client code so only the active locale's layers reach the browser.
Replace the seven local plural helpers with the ICU formatter based on Intl.PluralRules and add a lint rule against local plural helpers.
Derive the Intl tag from language and country (en with US gives en-US, es with US gives es-US, en with GB gives en-GB) instead of the fixed map.
Move remaining hard-coded visible strings (calendar export location, provider default name in the web app) to locale keys.
acceptance: Parallel requests in different languages never mix strings (tested).
The largest client chunk contains at most one language's dictionary.
English shows correct forms for 1, 2, 21 and 101; a US visitor sees month-day dates.
Locale parity and leak tests still pass.

packages.title: Locale files per feature namespace
packages.goal: Split the application dictionaries into locale-first namespace files so feature packages add their own strings in new files and never edit a shared dictionary.
steps: Move apps/web/app/_lib/locales/<locale>.json to apps/web/locales/<locale>/<namespace>.json (namespaces such as core, public, auth, workspace, assistant, demo) without changing any key or text.
Load only the namespaces a route needs on the server and pass only those layers to the client; keep the English fallback per namespace.
Extend the parity and leak tests to discover namespaces by listing the directories, so a new namespace file is checked automatically in every engine language.
Document the rule: a feature adds apps/web/locales/<locale>/<feature>.json for every engine language and never edits another feature's file.
acceptance: Every page renders byte-identical text before and after the move in all six languages (screenshot or text snapshot test).
A namespace missing in one language fails the parity test.
Client bundles contain only the namespaces the route uses.

packages.title: Asynchronous data boundary in the web app
packages.goal: Make every data function of the web app asynchronous and address entities by handle, still on fixtures, so the live API adapter can replace fixtures without touching pages again.
steps: Make the 30 exported adapter functions async and update every call site in public pages, workspace pages and components (mechanical change, no behaviour change).
Introduce the DataPort type that both the fixture adapter and the later HTTP adapter implement, keyed by handle for public pages and by id for workspace objects.
Remove stale comments that promise work BE-001 did not do; merge the three near-duplicate public assistant components into one parameterized component without changing behaviour.
Keep every browser test green.
acceptance: No page imports the fixture adapter directly; pages depend only on the DataPort.
The full browser suite passes unchanged.
A type test proves the fixture adapter satisfies the DataPort.

packages.title: Run the web app on the live API for accounts, companies and projects
packages.goal: Replace fixtures and the persona switch with the real API wherever the API exists, keeping an explicit demo mode for demo deployments.
steps: Add an HTTP adapter for the implemented endpoints behind the DataPort; route /v1/* to the API on the same origin (Next rewrite in development; reverse proxy in OPS-002) and forward cookies and the CSRF header.
Replace the fake auth handlers with the real sign-up, verification, login, recovery, step-up, sessions, memberships, company creation and projects flows; map every API error code to locale keys.
Introduce TRUSTWORK_DEMO_MODE: the persona switch and fixtures only when it is on; production builds refuse ?persona=.
Add an end-to-end Playwright suite against a seeded API and database in CI.
acceptance: With demo mode off, no fixture data or persona parameter influences any page (tested).
Sign-up, verified session, company creation and a published project work in the browser against the real API.
Every API error renders localized copy in every engine language; no raw code reaches the user.
Keyboard, screen reader and narrow-screen checks pass on the changed screens.

packages.title: Country pack v2 schema: facets, subdivisions, several time zones and identifiers, unit catalogue
packages.goal: Extend the pack schema so any country, including a federal one, is data: facets at country and subdivision level, each sourced and honestly verified.
steps: Extend the Zod schema with facets (registers, licensing, standards, procurement, tax and e-invoicing, e-signature, payments, calendar and holidays, units, scripts, privacy, content law, national sanctions lists, agent-law defaults) and verification levels; keep v1 fields compatible.
Allow subdivision-level facets and region kinds state, district and territory; several IANA time zones and several identifier kinds per pack.
Add a measurement-unit catalogue with explicit conversion rules (metric and imperial) in a units contract referenced by packs.
Extend the validator: sources required, rates as decimal strings, referenced adapters must exist, restricted places refused; update the country guide with facet instructions.
acceptance: Every fact requires a source and a verification level (validator test).
No pack can enable a restricted place.
The schema expresses a federal country with per-state facts (tested with a synthetic fixture, not real facts).
The four existing packs still validate unchanged.

packages.title: Sourced v2 facets for Uzbekistan, Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan
packages.goal: Keep the four example packs useful by adding v2 facts with primary sources, starting with registers, tax and e-invoicing.
steps: Research registers, tax and e-invoicing, e-signature, payments and holidays for UZ, GE, AM and AZ from primary sources.
Record each fact with source, retrieval date and verification level; mark secondary-source facts as pending official confirmation.
Name candidate verification adapters only as candidates; no live register call.
acceptance: All four packs validate under the v2 schema.
No fact without a source; unverified facts are labelled.
No Russian provider or payment rail appears in any pack.

packages.title: Configuration over code: runtime country packs, languages, defaults and brand
packages.goal: Let an operator add a country or a language and set the default country, languages and brand by configuration, without editing TypeScript or rebuilding.
steps: Load country packs and locale files from a configured data directory at start, validated with the existing schemas; refuse to start on invalid or restricted packs.

Replace DEFAULT_COUNTRY and fixed locale lists with deployment configuration (enabled countries, enabled languages, default language per country). With no configured country the engine has none: visitors get a neutral country choice and the setup wizard requires one (ADR 012).
Move the brand overlay, site URL and base path from build arguments to runtime configuration where Next allows it, and document the remainder.
Define the configuration file format so HUB-001 can later version it per hub with second-person activation; update the add-a-country guide so the happy path needs no code change.
acceptance: A new pack and a new language dropped into the data directory appear after a restart with no code change (tested).
One image serves two deployments with different default countries and brands.
Restricted places are refused at load.
Engine code contains no country-specific branch or default (lint or test).

packages.title: Spanish (es) as the seventh engine language
packages.goal: Spanish across the interface and demo content through configuration only, so the US hub and Latin American hubs can serve Spanish-speaking professionals; formats follow the country (es-US in the US hub).
steps: Add es files for every namespace in apps/web/locales/es and the design system dictionary packages/ui/locales/es.json with full key coverage and CLDR plural forms.
Add es overrides for the demo content.
Register es through configuration (no TypeScript change) and extend the locale and leak tests to es.
Label the translation machine-assisted until a native speaker reviews it; open a review request.
acceptance: No missing or placeholder keys in es; the brand reads Trustwork.
Every public page renders in es without Russian or untranslated text (leak test).
With country US, dates and numbers use es-US formats.
Status labels the review state honestly.

packages.title: United States country pack
packages.goal: A complete, sourced US pack that the reference hub runs on: the model for every other country.
steps: Regions: 50 states, the District of Columbia and the territories with ISO 3166-2 codes and correct kinds; several IANA time zones; US address order with a second address line and ZIP or ZIP+4; phone +1; USD.

Identifiers: EIN as the company identifier; state entity numbers, state contractor licence references and the SAM.gov UEI as additional identifier kinds with verification recipe references (no live register calls); entity forms (sole proprietorship, partnership, LLC, C and S corporation, nonprofit).

Facets: state contractor licensing boards, state sales tax treatment as data with a tax adapter reference, SAM.gov and state procurement portals, ESIGN and UETA notes, card and ACH rails, CCPA/CPRA and other state privacy regimes, federal holidays with observed-date rules, imperial units, agent-law defaults left unverified until counsel review.
Every fact with a primary source and verification level; locales en (and es once LANG-ES is done).
acceptance: The pack validates; no fact without a source; unverified facts are labelled.
A US visitor sees en-US formats, USD and the correct state list.
No engine code branches on US.

packages.title: United States demo hub: defaults and synthetic demo data
packages.goal: The reference deployment opens as a US hub in English (Spanish second) with synthetic, clearly labelled demo data, while the other countries stay selectable examples.
steps: Create a synthetic US dataset for one metro area (people, companies, projects with plans, events, publications, magazine issues, courses) with no real names, licences or EINs; obviously fictitious identifiers marked synthetic and example.invalid domains.
Personas for a US general contractor, a sole-proprietor subcontractor, a homeowner and a buyer.
Configure the demo deployment to US, English and Spanish through CFG-001; keep UZ, GE, AM and AZ selectable; select the dataset by configuration.
Update smoke and browser tests so they do not assume Uzbekistan as the default; record screenshots.
acceptance: A first visit to the demo shows the US hub in English with USD and month-day dates.
Every demo record is labelled synthetic; no real company or person appears.
Tests pass with US and with UZ as the configured default.

packages.title: Container images and a full local stack with same-origin routing
packages.goal: Produce deployable, non-root images for web, API, worker and migrations and a compose stack that mirrors the production topology.
steps: Multi-stage images: web with Next standalone output, API and worker without dev dependencies, all non-root with health checks.
A one-shot migration image or command that runs as the migrator role, never as the runtime role.
Extend infra/compose.yaml with API, worker, web, S3-compatible object storage and a reverse proxy that serves one origin and routes /v1/* to the API.
Document runtime configuration (no secrets in images) and produce an SBOM per image; build images in CI for pull requests that touch apps, packages or infra. Do not deploy anywhere.
acceptance: docker compose up brings a working stack where sign-up and login work through the proxy on one origin.
Images run as a non-root user and contain no devDependencies, tests or docs.
Images build in CI.

packages.title: Shared kernel persistence: files, units, jurisdictions, taxonomy, exchange rates and the hub anchor
packages.goal: Create the shared tables every later slice references, so modules never invent their own file, unit, jurisdiction, taxonomy or hub columns.
steps: Add evidence_artifact with classification, hash, scan state and parent reference.
Add unit, unit_conversion_rule, jurisdiction (loaded from country packs by a maintenance command, restricted flag computed from code) and exchange_rate_snapshot.
Add taxonomy_term (including the plan-step schemes work_type, trade, material, stage and skill), step_term_relation and taxonomy_release with engine and hub scope.
Add a minimal hub and hub_territory anchor (id, node-local key, status, pack binding) that HUB-001 extends.
acceptance: A restricted jurisdiction cannot be inserted as a hub territory or selectable region (tested).
Unit conversion happens only through an explicit rule; quantities with different units never add.
US, UZ, GE, AM and AZ jurisdictions load from packs only; no SQL literal of a real-world fact.
Every table is mirrored in packages/data/src/schema/kernel.ts and covered by the introspection test.

packages.title: Object storage port and attachments
packages.goal: Store files (avatars, publication images, magazine PDFs, project and evidence attachments) with classification inherited from their parent.
steps: Contracts for attachment metadata, classification and upload and download commands.
A BlobStore port with an S3-compatible adapter and a filesystem fake; content hashes, size and type limits.
Upload through short-lived signed URLs; download only through an authorized parent check with bounded TTL.
A scanning port (fake) and a quarantine state before a file becomes visible; deletion and erasure through the worker with tombstones for restore replay.
acceptance: A participant without access to the parent cannot obtain a URL for its attachment (negative tests).
Copy or move preserves owner and classification and is audited.
No external storage account is created by this package.

packages.title: Administration persistence
packages.goal: Add platform-administration tables as reviewed migrations with append-only grants, scoped to platform, node or hub.
steps: Migrations go in packages/data/migrations/admin, which the runner reads after DATA-004 (the earlier admin subdirectory was never read by the flat runner).
Create audit and access-log tables with INSERT-only grants and raising triggers.

Create staff role definitions and assignments with scope platform, node or hub (ADR 012), second-person approvals, case grants, support cases, moderation, sanctions, appeals, feature flags, maintenance windows, incidents and kill switches (claims move to CLM-001).
acceptance: The runtime role cannot update or delete audit rows (tested).
Requester and approver must differ; case grants expire within 72 hours.
No columns are added to other modules' tables.
Every new migration file is applied by npm run db:migrate in a test.

packages.title: Platform administration backend module
packages.goal: Audited staff authority, separation-of-duties modes, case grants, moderation and the admin use-case facade that calls other modules' use cases only.
steps: Materialise admin.* grants and separation-of-duties evaluation for platform, node and hub scopes.
Elevated sessions (BE-004), second-person approval bound to an action digest, case and dispute-case grants.
Moderation reports, cases, sanction ladder and appeals so user-generated content can go public.
Facade use cases with fakes for modules not yet accepted; real-PostgreSQL negative tests.
acceptance: Invariants pass under the runtime role.
No endpoint accepts a ranking weight, score, position or badge.
No module imports platform-admin.
A sanction of level 4 needs a second person (tested).

packages.title: Platform release candidate: the US demo hub on a deployable stack
packages.goal: Prove the platform phase outcome on synthetic data before any deployment proposal: a person signs up, verifies by e-mail, creates a company, invites a colleague, creates and publishes a project and sees it on the public site of the US demo hub.
steps: Run the end-to-end journey against the compose stack with the SMTP sink, in English and Spanish, at desktop and phone width.
Run negative authorization, readiness and worker fault suites at the exact head commit.
Record limitations, provider modes (fake or live) and the owner decisions still needed before a deployment (hosting, operator entity, privacy notices).
acceptance: Named, non-empty CI run at the exact head commit with test counts.
The journey passes with demo mode off; no fixture data appears.
A written gate list for the owner; no deployment happens in this package.

packages.title: Profiles, consent records, portraits and experience
packages.goal: Give every person a lifelong, consent-driven public profile with experience, and a recorded consent for every public mention.
steps: Add person_profile, person_preference, consent_record, media_licence, portrait, experience_entry, follow, bookmark and reading_progress (portfolio entries and credentials belong to REP-001).
Implement consent withdrawal that unpublishes dependent projections in the same transaction and emits tombstones.
Expose public profile reads only through allowlisted serializers; extend forbidden-field tests.
Connect the «Моя страница» public profile editor and the people directory pages to the API.
acceptance: A person mentioned or listed without consent never appears publicly (tested).
A portrait is shown only with both consent and a licence record.
Reading progress and bookmarks are never visible to employers or colleagues.
Experience entries belong to the person and survive employment changes.

packages.title: Context threads, messages, notifications, channel grants and templates
packages.goal: Conversations that belong to the work, notifications that never leak, and versioned templates in every hub language.
steps: Add context_thread, message, message_link, reply_token, channel_grant, send_receipt, notification, notification_preference, message_template, template_version, delivery, sender_identity and suppression_entry.
Implement idempotent inbound intake keyed by provider message id; inbound content is flagged untrusted and never issues commands.
Block template activation unless every hub language exists and the activator differs from the drafter; fake mail and messenger adapters only.
Connect the notifications page and bell to the API.
acceptance: No thread exists without a context; non-participants get not found (tested).
Duplicate inbound events never create duplicate messages.
A notification never carries a value the recipient may not read (forbidden-field test).
Suppressed addresses never receive non-transactional mail.

packages.title: Publications, corrections and curated issues: backend
packages.goal: Build the sourced publication lifecycle and the weekly curated issue on PostgreSQL behind the frozen content contracts.
steps: Add publication, version, authorship, correction, topics, entity links, edition links, wall references, comments, issue, issue revision, issue item, render artifact and magazine digest (packages/data/migrations/content).
Implement author versus editor rights, moderation holds (ADM-001) and source and time labels for news.
Curate numbered and dated issues with frozen publication versions and an archive; corrections create visible revisions.
Validate correction, retraction, publication permissions and source licensing in tests.
acceptance: Published versions and released issues are immutable; a correction is a new version (tested).
Author and editor rights are distinct; a moderation hold removes the public projection.
No invented recurring journal paywall or public traction claim.

packages.title: News, articles and the magazine on the API, with the PDF layout
packages.goal: Serve news, articles and the magazine from the API with a responsive reader and a separately laid-out PDF edition.
steps: Wire the news, articles, magazine and publications pages to the API through the DataPort.
Build the PDF layout pipeline as a worker job producing a render artifact per issue revision.
Keep RSS feeds and rubric pages working from the API.
acceptance: The magazine is a curated issue; mobile readable; the PDF is inspected page by page in the pull request.
Every page passes keyboard, screen reader and narrow-screen checks in every engine language.
A corrected publication shows its correction note in web, feed and the next PDF render.

packages.title: Open plan-step taxonomy v1 (CC0) with slots for licensed mappings
packages.goal: Publish the shared vocabulary that plans, consultations, tasks, knowledge and recommendations use: work types, trades, materials, stages and skills with predecessors, under CC0.
steps: Write the plan-step taxonomy as data in data/taxonomy (codes stable once released, English labels as reference, other languages through locale files) with predecessor relations and permit and inspection question keys per country pack.
Add crosswalk slots to IFC and ETIM classes and to proprietary classifications; proprietary crosswalks are hub-licensed data, never shipped in the repository.
Add a validator (unique codes, acyclic predecessors, every label key present in English) and a licence file (CC0 1.0).
Cover the US single-family house build end to end as the worked example (synthetic, no code citations claimed as verified).
acceptance: The taxonomy validates in npm run check; codes are stable and documented.
The engine works without any proprietary classification licence.
No real-world code requirement is presented as verified without a source.

packages.title: Project plans: versions, items, dependencies, changes, sharing with invited experts, permits and diaries
packages.goal: Turn a project into a plan the owner approves (phases, tasks, trades, materials, permits and inspections, budget ranges, timeline, risks, decision points) and keep every version and change, so nobody is blamed retroactively.
steps: Contracts first: plan, plan_version with statuses draft, proposed, approved and superseded (ADR 012), plan_item keyed by the plan-step taxonomy, plan_dependency, plan_item_state, plan_change, plan_share, permit_record, project_diary_entry and project_location.
Migrations in packages/data/migrations/plans; a proposed version freezes; approval is the owner's act; agents may only propose versions under a mandate.
Implement plan_share as participation rows with the invited-plan serializer; extend forbidden-field tests (budgets, notes, other invitees, address before booking).
Validate dependency graphs as acyclic; expose plan changes to EXE-001 for timing attribution; show which steps a state or country requires a licensed professional for, from the pack.
acceptance: Approved plan versions are immutable; original and revised versions are both retained (tested).
An invited expert sees exactly the shared items and fields; uninvited parties get not found (negative tests).
A plan and its unshared items never appear in search, notifications, other parties' views or federation.
Budget ranges are shown as ranges with their basis and never as quotes.

packages.title: Catalogue, needs, RFQs and invitations (commerce slice 1)
packages.goal: Deliver the buyer side up to invitations: reusable versioned offerings, needs, RFQs with immutable published versions and invitations pinned to them.
steps: Rebase the draft migrations of pull request #36 into packages/data/migrations/commerce after DATA-003 (units and kernel) and review them.
Implement versioned offerings (catalogue) separate from quote snapshots; private floors never published.
Implement needs, RFQ drafts, publication of immutable RFQ versions and invitations that pin rfq_version_id.
Implement amendments that flag stale responses and the ownership helpers for commercial resource kinds.
acceptance: Invitations bind the exact RFQ version; an amendment flags stale responses (tested).
A catalogue edit cannot change a sent quote or an accepted agreement.
Buyer budget and private constraints never reach sellers (forbidden-field tests).
Mixed goods, works and services lines with explicit units are supported.

packages.title: Quotes, negotiation, agreements and orders (commerce slice 2)
packages.goal: Complete the paired flow: quote versions against the current RFQ version, normalization and comparison, negotiation rounds, agreements, acceptance and orders, with the agreement kinds tasks and consultations need.
steps: Migrations in packages/data/migrations/transactions: quote, quote_version, quote_line, quote_private_constraint, tax_determination, negotiation_round, amendment_request, agreement with terms_kind (rfq_quote, task, consultation; ADR 012), private agreement halves, acceptance_event, order, order_change and obligation.
Implement quote snapshots only against the published current RFQ version and comparison normalization with explicit exclusions.
Implement selection, agreement and order commands with authority checks and two-party projections; acceptance recomputes digests.
Electronic acceptance records consent to electronic records as configured per hub (ESIGN and UETA notes in the US pack).
acceptance: An old quote against quantity 10 in v1 cannot be compared or accepted as quantity 100 in v2 (tested).
Accepted terms are identical for both parties by digest; private halves never cross.
Optimistic concurrency and duplicate acceptance tests pass on real PostgreSQL.

packages.title: Consultations and mentoring from plan items
packages.goal: Let a plan item become a consultation request (advice session, review of drawings or quotes, site visit) or a mentoring series with an expert: scoped, scheduled, free or priced, with an accepted deliverable.
steps: Contracts and migrations (packages/data/migrations/consultations): consultation_offering on catalogue offerings, availability_window, consultation_request, consultation_booking, consultation_session, consultation_deliverable and mentoring_relationship.
Bookings are agreements with terms_kind consultation; booked terms are immutable and digest-bound; capacity is serialized against availability.
Scheduling with calendar files and reminders through context threads; the site address is revealed only after a site-visit booking.
Priced consultations show the full price and the hub's commission before booking; charging is CONS-002.
acceptance: Booked consultation terms are immutable and digest-bound (tested).
A budget ceiling of the requester never reaches the expert (forbidden-field test).
Licence-requiring advice is offered only by experts whose licence is recorded (checked once CLM-001 lands; self-declared until then and labelled so).
Deliverables are visible only to the parties unless the author publishes them.

packages.title: Scoped tasks from plan items for contractors and trades
packages.goal: Let plan items become scoped task requests to contractors and trades, reusing RFQs, quote versions, agreements and execution records.
steps: Contracts and migrations (packages/data/migrations/tasks): task_request, task_request_version, task_offer, task_offer_private and task_assignment mapped onto RFQ and quote versions.
Agreements with terms_kind task; milestones from plan items; evidence through execution records.
Competing offerors are isolated; the address is revealed only after assignment.
Reviews are allowed only for completed tasks.
acceptance: Sent task offers are immutable and digest-bound (tested).
Competing offerors never see each other's offers (negative test).
A task assignment always names the plan item and the agreement version.

packages.title: Project execution and fair reputation
packages.goal: Implement evidence-aware execution, partial fulfilment and acceptance, and an explainable reputation prototype.
steps: Preserve baseline and change attribution from plan versions and plan changes.
Record claims, evidence, confirmations, disputes and supersession independently (packages/data/migrations/execution).
Support goods delivery and works or services acceptance and defects.
Prototype dimension and sample methodology and the appeal workflow with synthetic fixtures.
acceptance: A client-caused plan change cannot automatically penalize the supplier (tested).
Missing evidence is not failure; subjective review stays distinct from fact.
Paying cannot improve reputation; private evidence is not public by default.

packages.title: Reputation builder: credentials, portfolio, confirmations, contributions and timeliness
packages.goal: Give every participant tools to build and confirm their own reputation from evidence: credentials, an evidence-backed portfolio, confirmations from real counterparties, knowledge contributions and timeliness signals, never paid and never surveillance.
steps: Contracts and migrations (packages/data/migrations/reputation): professional_credential (licences, insurance, bonds, certificates, training) for people and companies, portfolio_entry, confirmation_request, confirmation_response, contribution_record and timeliness_observation.
Allow confirmations only from parties of an accepted agreement, completed booking or closed project; block employees and relatives of the subject; no incentives; one request plus one reminder.
Let a participant invite a former client to confirm a past project; evidence exists only after confirmation; self-reported and client-confirmed are labelled differently.
Derive contributions and timeliness from canonical records only; every observation is visible to its subject and appealable.
acceptance: A confirmation without a recorded relationship is rejected (negative test).
No entitlement, payment, sponsorship or staff action changes a snapshot (comparison test).
No input comes from activity tracking or per-employee metrics.
Client-caused delay is excluded from timeliness.

packages.title: Shared knowledge from completed projects: diaries, lessons, checklists, templates and Q&A
packages.goal: With the owner's consent, turn completed projects into shared knowledge others learn from, under a licence the author chooses, with provenance and redaction review.
steps: Add knowledge_item, knowledge_consent and template_derivation (packages/data/migrations/knowledge); publication formats diary, lesson, checklist, template and expert answer linked to the source project version.
Require the project owner's consent and each named participant's consent or anonymization; a redaction step strips budgets, prices, addresses, faces and private data of counterparties.
Add a licence per item (for example CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0, all rights reserved) shown to readers and carried in exports and federation.
Let a person start a new plan from a published template with attribution; show the formats in the reader and on the project.
acceptance: Nothing from a private project is published without the owner's publish act and recorded consents (tested).
Consent withdrawal unpublishes or re-anonymizes the item and emits tombstones.
Templates keep a link to their source and author; the licence travels with every copy.

packages.title: Plan to people on the web: plan editor, step requests, consultations and tasks
packages.goal: Show the flagship journey in the workspace: a project's plan with versions and changes, items that become consultation or task requests, bookings and offers, in every engine language.
steps: Write screen contracts for the plan view, item request, booking and offer screens with empty, error, denied and mobile states.
Build the plan view (phases, items, dependencies, budget ranges with basis, decisions) and the version and change history.
Build item-to-request flows for consultations and tasks and the consultations list; strings in a new locale namespace for every engine language.
Playwright journeys at three widths with axe checks.
acceptance: An invited expert's view shows only shared items (browser test with two personas).
Every action that sends something names its recipient and needs an explicit act.
Keyboard, screen reader and 375 px checks pass.

packages.title: Reputation builder on the web
packages.goal: Let every participant see, build and present their reputation: credentials with expiry, portfolio, confirmations, contributions, timeliness and appeals, with explanations.
steps: Screen contracts for the reputation tab on «Моя страница» and the company page, public reputation cards and the appeal flow.
Build the screens on the API with explanations of every signal (method version, sample size, exclusions).
Strings in a new locale namespace for every engine language; Playwright and axe at three widths.
acceptance: Self-reported, client-confirmed and checked items are visually and textually distinct.
No screen shows a score without its method and sample size.
No paid upgrade is offered anywhere near reputation.

packages.title: Hub business-model playbook and the public price-transparency page design
packages.goal: Document acceptable and forbidden revenue options for hubs under ADR 010 decisions 20 and 21 and design the public page that lists every active price version, fee and commission and what payment never buys.
steps: Write the playbook section: capacity subscriptions, per-action agent pricing, deliverables, event and course marketplaces, consultation and task commissions as versioned hub settings, verification at cost, labelled sponsorship (off by default).
List forbidden models: per-lead fees, paid ranking, paid badges, selling attendee or profile-view data, holding participants' money.
Design the public price page contract and its empty and error states.
acceptance: Every option names the invariant that keeps payment away from ranking, matching, recommendations and reputation.
npm run validate:docs passes.
Owner or maintainer review recorded before status changes.

packages.title: Neutral offers, entitlements and two budget kinds
packages.goal: Separate platform service charges from commercial transaction budgets with versioned prices.
steps: Migrations in packages/data/migrations/billing: billing_account, offer, subscription_plan_version, price_version, price_acceptance, subscription, entitlement, meter, meter_rate_version, marketplace_fee_version, usage_record, budget, reservation, ledger_entry and credit_grant.
Define synthetic offer and price versions; never invent real prices.
Implement entitlement checks, price acceptance and the atomic reservation and ledger port for personal and company payers and project or employee scopes.
Test concurrent reserve, refund, correction and expiry.
acceptance: Transaction authority never implies a paid-platform budget.
Concurrent reservations cannot exceed the balance; no float money (tested).
Free basic participation for both sides; activator differs from drafter for price versions.
No provider registration, payment or actual charge.

packages.title: Payment provider port: licensed providers only, webhook inbox and reconciliation
packages.goal: Connect charges, escrow and payouts to a provider-neutral port that a hub configures with licensed providers (cards and ACH for the US hub); Trustwork records instructions, references, evidence and reconciliation and never holds, pools or moves funds itself (ADR 010 decision 20).
steps: Define the payment port (create intent, confirm, refund, payout through the provider's connected accounts, lookup outcome) and a deterministic fake.
Process provider webhooks idempotently through inbox_receipt; reconcile unknown outcomes instead of retrying.
Tie payments to BILL-001 reservations and ledger entries in integer minor units; store provider references, never card or bank data.
Keep rails configurable per hub; refuse configurations that would route funds through an account of the operator; no Russian providers or rails; no account registration or real charge.
acceptance: Duplicate and out-of-order webhooks never double-settle (tests).
A timeout leaves the payment in outcome_unknown until reconciliation.
No code path credits a balance held by Trustwork or the hub operator (test and review checklist).
Ranking, matching, recommendation and reputation code has no dependency on payment state (tested).

packages.title: Invoices, tax determinations, refunds and payouts through licensed providers
packages.goal: Charge for tickets, courses, consultations and platform services with reproducible per-jurisdiction tax and pay organizers, authors and experts through the provider, never through a Trustwork balance.
steps: Add invoice, invoice_line, refund, payout_account (provider references only) and payout (packages/data/migrations/invoicing).
Determine tax from country-pack rules or a tax adapter and store the rule reference and jurisdiction (US sales tax per state, county and city as the worked example, fake adapter).
Screen payees with the compliance package before the first payout; payout fees come from a published price version.
Reconcile unknown outcomes; balanced ledger entries for every money movement.
acceptance: Every tax amount names its jurisdiction and rule source; no hard-coded rate.
A payment timeout never produces a second charge.
Card and bank data never enter the database.

packages.title: Hub commissions and fees as versioned, disclosed settings
packages.goal: Let the hub administrator set commissions and fees (consultations, tasks, marketplace categories, events, courses, agent capacity) as versioned price records with second-person activation, an effective date and public disclosure (ADR 010 decision 21).
steps: Implement commission and fee versions on marketplace_fee_version with category scope, effective dates and no overlapping active versions.
Second-person activation and an audit record; participants accept the version in force at booking or acceptance.
Build the public price page from BIZ-001's design listing every active price, fee and commission and what payment never buys.
Comparison tests: ranking, matching, recommendations and reputation are identical with and without commissions.
acceptance: A fee version cannot be activated by its drafter (tested).
Every booking or acceptance records the fee version shown before confirmation.
The public price page lists every active version in every hub language.

packages.title: Paid consultations and mentoring through the payment provider
packages.goal: Charge priced consultations and mentoring series through the hub's licensed payment provider with full price, commission and refund terms shown before confirmation.
steps: Charge at booking or after the deliverable according to the offering version; refunds follow the cancellation terms.
Recurring mentoring charges only with an explicit, separately confirmed recurring term and one-click cancellation.
Reconcile unknown outcomes; payouts to experts through the provider.
acceptance: No recurring charge exists without a separately confirmed recurring term (test).
Paid status never changes an expert's rank in matching or recommendations (comparison test).
Funds never pass through a Trustwork or operator balance.

packages.title: Getting paid: pay applications, retainage, lien waivers and payment-timeliness evidence
packages.goal: Model payment milestones and pay applications under agreements, retainage with release conditions, statutory lien-waiver exchange bound to actual payments, prompt-payment reminders from pack facts and timeliness evidence for both sides, with funds handled only by licensed providers.
steps: Define pay application, retainage ledger, lien waiver (conditional or unconditional, progress or final) and payment-event contracts bound by digest to agreement versions.
Store statutory waiver templates and retainage and prompt-payment facts per state as reviewed pack data (US worked example, unverified until counsel review).
Release an unconditional waiver only against cleared-payment evidence from PAY-001.
Record due and paid dates as timeliness evidence for both parties.
acceptance: An unconditional waiver cannot be issued before cleared-payment evidence (test).
Concurrent releases cannot exceed the milestone amount or the remaining retainage.
Financing partners, if shown, are labelled and never change ranking or reputation.

packages.title: Commercial experiences: procurement and sales on the API
packages.goal: Implement complete buyer and seller flows in the workspace with exact snapshots, authority and budgets.
steps: Build intake, clarification, compare, version and acceptance flows with exact snapshots.
Show structured authority, budget, approvals and unknown or pending outcomes.
Validate mixed workflows and narrow-screen tables against the API; strings in a new locale namespace.
acceptance: No docked reflowing panel or Agents navigation.
Stale quotes against an amended RFQ are visibly not comparable.
Mobile, keyboard, empty, error and denial states verified; no approval claimed from a screenshot.

packages.title: Field evidence: RFIs, submittals, change orders, daily logs, punch lists and photos
packages.goal: Add versioned field records that matter as evidence so fair timing and reputation rest on what happened on site.
steps: Define the record contracts with immutable versions, authorship, project participation and digests.
Link change orders to agreement amendments and RFIs to delay attribution.
Store photos with capture time and optional location; strip location and faces from any public projection.
acceptance: Records are visible only to project participants with the right capability (negative tests).
Daily logs carry no per-worker productivity fields.
Public views never include photo location metadata.

packages.title: Dispute evidence packages and mediation referral
packages.goal: Let parties assemble a dispute package (digest-bound agreement versions, change orders, field records, payments, waivers, messages in context) and refer it to an external mediator; outcomes enter reputation only as consented, cited evidence.
steps: Define the package manifest with digests and an export both parties can verify.
Add a referral step to configured external providers; Trustwork never decides the dispute.
Annotate affected reputation observations while a dispute is open.
acceptance: A package contains only records both parties are entitled to see (negative test).
Digests in the export verify against the stored versions.
Outcomes enter reputation only as consented, cited evidence.

packages.title: Review and freeze the hub console contracts
packages.goal: Accept packages/contracts/src/hub.ts as the console contract: hub, modes, launch gates, configuration versions, providers and secret references, routing, egress, budgets, kill switches, sources, datasets, links, schedules, pipelines, runs, editorial items, agent product, plan to people, credentials, recommendations, setup and support.
steps: Review naming against docs/data/model.md (snake_case tables, projection layers, Party XOR, versioned records) and record differences.
Merge HUB_CONSOLE_PERMISSIONS and HUB_SECOND_PERSON_ACTIONS into the admin vocabulary with staff scope platform, node or hub (ADR 012).
Add the decision 22 shapes the console needs: jurisdiction settings domain and agent extension version references (full schemas live in HUB-005 and AGT-023).
Generate JSON Schema for the console contracts.
acceptance: Every invariant in hub.ts has a positive and a negative test.
No schema carries a secret value except the write-only submit command.
No permission or field can set a score, position, badge or ranking weight (tested).

packages.title: Hubs, territories, hub-scoped staff and versioned hub configuration
packages.goal: Make the hub a first-class object: territory, lifecycle, hub-scoped staff roles and configuration versions activated by a second person; the deployment configuration of CFG-001 becomes the hub's first configuration version.
steps: Extend the hub anchor of DATA-003 with territory, hub_config_version, legal_document_version, counsel_approval, legal_acceptance, launch_gate, provider_credential_ref, retention_policy (packages/data/migrations/hubs).
Scope staff role assignments and audit to a hub or node.
Implement second-person activation for sensitive configuration domains and the hub lifecycle with launch gates that block going public.
Refuse restricted territories at every entry point; import CFG-001 deployment settings as configuration version 1.
acceptance: A hub cannot go public with an open launch gate (tested).
A restricted territory is rejected.
Sensitive configuration changes require a different approver.
No hub setting widens data access.

packages.title: Jurisdiction settings: agent disclosure, liability, consent, record-keeping and per-action limits
packages.goal: Follow each country's law through configuration (ADR 010 decision 22): agent disclosure wording, liability allocation for agent commitments, consent and record-keeping, limits per action type and legal texts are per-hub and per-jurisdiction settings with sourced country-pack defaults, versioned and audited.
steps: Contracts for a jurisdiction settings domain of hub configuration: disclosure text keys per language, liability allocation options, consent and record-keeping rules, per-action limits and approval requirements, each with the pack default and its source.
Resolve the effective setting for a participant, an action and a counterparty jurisdiction (most protective wins when two apply).
Second-person activation and audit; a hub can be stricter than the pack default but never weaker than a mandatory pack rule.
Expose the resolver to the agent runtime and to participant agent settings (AGT-022) as read-only limits.
acceptance: Changing the disclosure text needs every hub language and a second person (tested).
An action above a jurisdiction limit requires approval even under a mandate that would allow it (tested).
No engine code contains a country-specific legal rule; defaults come from packs.

packages.title: Setup wizard backend and first run
packages.goal: Turn a fresh node into a configured draft hub: setup token, node identity, hub identity from a country pack or the generic profile (a country is required; ADR 012), operator screening, first administrator with a second factor, residency, fake providers, modes.
steps: Implement setup token issuance, hashing, expiry and single use.
Implement the setup state transitions in order with resumable steps; the country step is mandatory.
Create hub, territories, configuration versions and launch gates; refuse restricted territories at every level; offer OpenRouter as one optional provider next to direct providers (ADR 012).
Require a second factor for the first administrator and issue recovery codes.
acceptance: A second setup cannot start after setup finished (tested).
A restricted country, region or place is refused.
The first administrator cannot finish without a second factor.

packages.title: Provider connections, secret store, model routes, egress, spending caps and kill switches
packages.goal: Let operators connect their own providers safely: write-only secrets with envelope encryption, synthetic connection tests, routing per job with fallbacks, default-deny egress by data class and residency, caps and kill switches.
steps: Implement the secret store port with envelope encryption and an external KMS or Vault adapter interface; fake adapter for tests.
Implement connection tests that send only synthetic input.
Implement route resolution with fallbacks and the egress decision function every model or provider call must pass.
Implement caps with a hard stop and kill switches with two-person release.
acceptance: No API response, log line, audit event or outbox payload contains a secret value (tested by scanning).
A call with a non-public data class to a connection without an allow rule is refused.
An exhausted cap blocks new paid calls.

packages.title: Counterparty verification adapters, recipes and sanctions list configuration
packages.goal: Turn local registers and sanctions lists into evidence: check adapters in fake, manual and live modes, recipes per subject and trigger, results with retention and appeals.
steps: Define check-type contracts (register match, officer match, tax status, licence, qualification, ownership, sanctions, domain, signature, call-back).
Implement adapters with deterministic fakes and a manual-review mode; live mode behind second-person activation and KEYS-001 secret references.
Implement recipes, result evidence records, expiry and re-check scheduling (packages/data/migrations/verification).
Implement potential-match review cases and appeals decided by a different reviewer; map results to badge categories and eligibility flags.
acceptance: Baseline sanctions screening cannot be disabled.
A potential match never auto-blocks or auto-clears.
Badges show categories, never documents; results expire and trigger re-checks per recipe.

packages.title: Company identifiers, registrations, licences, claims and per-hub verification badges
